checks.description: Three-level FIFO and partial-fill tape matches a manually calculated oracle.
checks.evidence: Expected fills: 3@101 from order 1, 4@101 from order 2, 1@102 from order 3; 4 lots remain at 102.
checks.limitation: Visible-book, price-time-priority mechanics only; hidden liquidity is outside this mode.

checks.description: Fixed seven-stage latency path equals manual nanosecond addition.
checks.limitation: This validates composition and causal timestamps, not empirical latency calibration.

checks.description: Identical seed/config is byte deterministic and a changed seed changes the tape.
checks.evidence: Repeated SHA-256 equality for seed 42 and inequality against seed 43.
checks.limitation: Determinism is conditional on the documented software/configuration contract.

checks.description: Invalid configuration and post-generation tape mutation are rejected.
checks.evidence: Zero grid interval rejected; canonical action mutation invalidates tape verification.
checks.limitation: Failure injection is deterministic mutation testing, not exhaustive adversarial fuzzing.

checks.description: Sixty-four generated seeds preserve tape accounting and non-crossed-book invariants.
checks.evidence: 16,384 generated grid steps; each tape passed independent validate_tape checks.
checks.limitation: Designed synthetic distributions are not evidence of historical goodness of fit.

checks.description: Structured mutation campaign detects corrupted configuration, sequence, accounting, hash and book fields.
checks.limitation: Deterministic structure-aware mutation is not coverage-guided libFuzzer execution.

checks.description: Independent deque/map reference book agrees with the production engine over 64,000 commands.
checks.evidence: 32 seeds x 2,000 valid limit, market and cancel commands matched after every command.
checks.limitation: Reference covers visible FIFO limit/market/cancel semantics; replacement and exchange-specific rules retain dedicated tests.

sensitivities.description: Increasing market-order probability increases generated aggressive submissions.
Increasing target visible lots increases mean visible book depth.
Increasing reference-move frequency, jump size and impact raises absolute terminal displacement.
A liquidity-vacuum shock lowers minimum visible depth.

limitations: Gate B validates exact synthetic mechanics and designed-process responsiveness, not historical realism.
The Step 9 process remains explicitly uncalibrated until real data are selected and analysed.
Visible-book simulation omits hidden liquidity and venue-specific matching rules not yet selected.
Local TSan is unavailable because the installed Swift Clang runtime cannot link its libdispatch/Blocks interceptors.
Historical aggregate replay and queue-model validity remain future Gates C and later sensitivity work.
